primary_references.finding: The signal targets the calling process when its parent thread dies and the setting is cleared in a forked child.
An orphaned descendant is reparented to the nearest living subreaper, which can wait for it.
A forked child inherits its parent process group, but a process can later change grouping where permitted.
Duplicated descriptors share one flock and the lock persists until explicit unlock or the last duplicate closes.
A pidfd gives pollable identity and signal access for one process, not ownership of a descendant set.
Writing 1 to a non-root cgroup.kill kills the cgroup subtree and handles concurrent forks and migrations.
A control-group KillMode delegates unit process-set cleanup to the service manager, subject to manager and unit availability.

option_assessment.reason: It closes the direct-parent loss race for the Worker but does not propagate through fork.
It supports TERM then KILL for descendants that retain the Worker group, without extra privilege.
It lets the Guardian adopt and wait for orphaned Worker descendants.
It preserves current stdio and fixture boundaries while keeping cleanup and the render lock alive after host loss.
It strengthens Worker identity and exit observation but cannot define or kill the complete descendant set.
It is the stronger escape-resistant kill set, but no writable delegated per-render subtree is proven for this session.
It changes parent, stdio, lifecycle, and deployment assumptions and the current user manager is degraded.

selected_architecture.name: repository_owned_guardian

actors.host: Acquires admission, retains a fallback lock descriptor, records readiness, drives request and response, and cleans a known group if the Guardian alone fails.
actors.guardian: Runs outside the Worker group, becomes a child subreaper, retains the same lock open-file-description, owns Worker lifecycle, and survives Host EOF.
actors.worker_bootstrap: Sets parent-death SIGKILL and creates its session and group before waiting behind a start gate; payload exec is forbidden until the Host has acknowledged its PID and PGID.
actors.payload: Exec-replaces the bootstrap only after readiness and inherits neither the custody lock nor Guardian protocol descriptors.

selected_architecture.lock_invariant: Host and Guardian retain duplicate descriptors for the same flock open-file-description; neither may call LOCK_UN, and the final descriptor may close only after its surviving custodian has completed cleanup.
selected_architecture.liveness_invariant: The Host owns the sole control-channel write end; EOF is an unforgeable local Host-loss signal to the Guardian, while Guardian event EOF is the Host fallback trigger.
selected_architecture.termination_invariant: Every started path sends SIGTERM to the recorded Worker process group, waits the bounded grace, sends SIGKILL, and proves the group absent before releasing custody.
selected_architecture.reaping_invariant: The Guardian waits for the direct Worker and drains all orphan descendants adopted as subreaper before its lock descriptor closes.

single_fault_paths.host_lost: Guardian observes EOF, terminates the Worker group, reaps direct and adopted children, then closes its final lock descriptor.
single_fault_paths.guardian_lost_before_payload_start: Bootstrap parent-death handling prevents payload start; Host retains the lock and rejects the attempt.
single_fault_paths.guardian_lost_after_worker_identity: Host observes Guardian EOF, uses the recorded PGID for bounded group cleanup, proves absence, then closes its final lock descriptor.
single_fault_paths.normal_completion: Guardian reaps and proves group absence, closes its lock descriptor, and reports completion; Host closes its duplicate without LOCK_UN after accepting the terminal event.
